description:
This project is a short personal work completed during my free time over the course of one week. After several months without using Blender due to intensive CPGE studies, I took advantage of the holidays to return to 3D work and keep my skills sharp.
The project explores photorealism through an interior brutalist architecture scene. The largest part of the work was dedicated to creating the concrete materials, which were generated entirely procedurally inside the Shader Editor.

The scene setup was kept intentionally simple. Lighting is based on a single sky texture to provide natural illumination. A wide 30 mm focal length was chosen to emphasize the architectural forms, with an aperture of f/2.8 to introduce a subtle depth of field.

Rendering was done with Cycles at a resolution of 2000×3000 px using 1024 samples, with an average render time of approximately one hour per image. The final images were exported from Blender in EXR, using a linear Rec.709 workflow.

Post-production and compositing were carried out in DaVinci Resolve.

The project was produced on a system equipped with 16 GB of DDR5 memory, an Intel Core i7-12700H processor and an NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3050. A few months ago, I switched to Linux; this was my first project completed on Ubuntu, where I observed noticeable performance gains compared to Windows 11.
